items.name: Sherbrooke Falls walk, Dandenong Ranges NP
items.venue: Sherbrooke or O'Donohue Picnic Ground, near Kallista
items.note: Short rainforest walk through mountain ash and tree ferns to a small falls, best after spring rain; night deer-control closures run in parts of the park until 19 Nov, so keep it a daytime outing.

items.name: Sugarloaf Peak via Wells Cave Track, Cathedral Range State Park
items.when: Any day (not on Total Fire Ban days)
items.note: A scramble through Wells Caves to the 920 m top of the range; Parks Vic says spring and early summer bring native orchids and are ideal for longer hikes here. Hard, not for young kids.

items.name: Flinders Peak Lookout, You Yangs Regional Park
items.note: 450 steps and 200 m of climb to views over Melbourne and Geelong, an hour from the city; go early before the summer heat and crowds.

items.name: Ballarat-Skipton Rail Trail
items.venue: Ballarat to Skipton (parking at Smythesdale and Linton)
items.note: 54 km of mostly concrete and fine gravel through Smythesdale and Linton, with the old Nimons Bridge as the highlight; easy to do in sections.

items.name: Main Yarra Trail, Southbank to Westerfolds Park
items.note: About 33 km out along the river through Yarra Bend, mostly flat and sealed with a few short steep pinches; a classic long city ride straight from the CBD.

items.name: The Wallflowers: 30 Years of Bringing Down the Horse
items.note: Jakob Dylan's band on their first ever Australian tour, playing Bringing Down the Horse in full plus Tom Petty's Long After Dark front to back.

items.name: Suzi Quatro, with Baby Animals
items.note: A genuine 70s rock legend; the first night is already gone, so the 3 Dec show is the one to grab.

items.name: Death Cab for Cutie: I Built You A Tower Tour
items.note: This weekend: their first Melbourne show in more than seven years.

items.name: Khalid, with Newport
items.note: This weekend: his first Melbourne arena show since 2019.

items.name: Queens of the Stone Age, with Primus and Tropical Fuck Storm
items.note: Big rock night with Primus as a heavyweight support.

items.name: Weezer: The Gathering Tour, with Third Eye Blind and Fountains of Wayne
items.note: On sale now: Weezer's first full Australian headline run in 14 years, with two other 90s hit-makers on the bill.

items.name: Beck: Ride Lonesome Tour
items.note: Just announced, one show only in Australia; presale Fri 13 Nov 11am, general sale Mon 16 Nov 11am.

items.name: Powderfinger: The Encore Run
items.note: Two extra Melbourne nights went on sale 5 Nov and the Friday is already sold out; Something For Kate support.

items.name: Ali Wong
items.note: Emmy-winning US stand-up (Netflix specials, Beef) back with new material; tickets on sale since 23 Oct.

items.name: Michelle Buteau: The Surviving & Thriving Tour
items.note: Her first-ever Australian run; the US comic behind Netflix's Survival of the Thickest.

items.name: Urzila Carlson: That's Enough Already
items.note: Nine Palais nights for the South African-born, NZ-based comic after a sold-out 2026 tour; on sale now.

items.name: BBL|16: Melbourne Stars v Adelaide Strikers
items.note: First Big Bash game at the 'G this summer, and kids go free.

items.name: Melbourne Derby: Melbourne City v Melbourne Victory
items.note: The A-League's biggest local rivalry, a week before Christmas.

items.name: Throwdown 35: Melbourne United v SE Melbourne Phoenix
items.note: This Saturday: United have won both derbies so far this season and are going for 3 from 3.

items.name: Melbourne United v NZ Breakers (Indigenous Round)
items.note: Next United home game; after that it's Bullets on Sun 6 Dec (3pm) and JackJumpers on Sat 12 Dec (7:30pm).

items.name: SE Melbourne Phoenix v Cairns Taipans
items.note: A Sunday-afternoon game that suits kids; Phoenix are next home v Sydney Kings on Sat 19 Dec, 8pm.

items.name: Watershed: The Death of Dr Duncan (Opera Australia)
items.note: Neil Armfield's five-star oratorio (libretto co-written by Christos Tsiolkas) about the 1972 drowning that led SA to decriminalise homosexuality; 1 hr 40.

items.name: Mrs. Doubtfire: The Musical
items.note: News: the Australian premiere opens in under two weeks, a family-friendly comedy musical based on the film.

items.name: NGV Triennial 2026
items.note: The NGV's big free summer showcase of contemporary art and design opens in a month.

items.name: EMERGENCE[Y]
items.note: Final weeks: art meets science on adaptation, from a vertical city farm to coral soundscapes and fungal fashion.

items.name: Lifelike
items.note: News: opens next week, ACMI's big show on screen puppetry.

items.name: Diwali at Queen Victoria Market
items.note: This Saturday: dozens of Indian food stalls, dance and live music, all under cover.

items.name: Colours of Asia: Garden of Wonders
items.note: Lantern gardens, Asian street food and performances by the river from the Asia Street Food Festival team.

items.name: Good Food & Wine Show: Christmas Edition
items.note: A ticketed food-and-drink Christmas market, good for edible gifts.

items.name: QVM Christmas Night Market
items.note: News: first night is in under two weeks, with festive food, gifts and falling snow.
